mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted by markets as a signal of tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces the present value of future equity earnings, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25 percentage points over the past quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous quarter (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2%, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate the Fed to maintain higher policy rates to curb inflation, reducing growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate crosses above 2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during the inflation above 2% period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests a strengthening labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.05 over the 60-day window despite the trigger being active.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both GDPC1 (goods orders) and HOUST (housing starts) for two consecutive months indicates weakening demand, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases for two consecutive months and HOUST decreases for the same period
regime_hint: contraction in business and housing demand
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% while FEDFUNDS remains below 1% suggests the economy is growing faster than the central bank is tightening, which supports S&P 500 optimism and yields positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by more than 2% in a month and FEDFUNDS < 1%
regime_hint: supply-side expansion not offset by monetary tightening
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it signals a labor market softening that reduces wage growth expectations and leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the softening period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (money supply growth) for four consecutive months is interpreted as a deflationary trend, prompting investors to discount future cash flows more heavily and producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during the deflationary trend.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of rising consumer confidence as measured by a composite of monthly CPIAUCSL and HOUST, the S&P 500 exhibits positive 20-day forward returns regardless of other macro signals, indicating a non-standard risk factor at play.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and HOUST both increase over the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) when the confidence composite rises.
